name: Vertical Integration

claims.claim_text: PCB service businesses tend to integrate downstream in stages, starting with bare board fabrication and only later adding assembly.
claims.quote_verbatim: I mean, it's cool that it's integrated. I'm sure they're going for very full vertical integration, you know, all the way down to like the board assembly eventually.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Contests, Ham Radio & TWIT.tv - Ham, Spam, Thank You Ma'am

claims.claim_text: Cree's defensibility in silicon carbide LEDs came only partly from patents; owning the whole silicon carbide process was the barrier competitors could not replicate.
claims.quote_verbatim: But the other part of it is we vertically integrated. We started a company based on silicon carbide LEDs and silicon carbide electronics.
claims.speaker: John Edmond
claims.episode_title: An Interview with John Edmond - Luciferous LED Lucubrator

claims.claim_text: Cree ran the chain end to end from day one, taking in raw powders and gases and shipping finished retail light fixtures.
claims.quote_verbatim: We are vertically integrated from basically raw material, powders, gases
claims.speaker: John Edmond
claims.episode_title: An Interview with John Edmond - Luciferous LED Lucubrator

claims.claim_text: Cree extended forward into fixtures by acquiring a street-lighting company in Racine, Wisconsin employing 800 people building product in the USA.
claims.quote_verbatim: We just, we just bought a company up in Racine, Wisconsin called Rude Lighting and it's all street lighting. And we have 800 people up there
claims.speaker: John Edmond
claims.episode_title: An Interview with John Edmond - Luciferous LED Lucubrator

claims.claim_text: A component maker that integrates far enough downstream can end up consuming its own components internally rather than selling them on the merchant market.
claims.quote_verbatim: So I would hope someday we would just be making everything for internal use.
claims.speaker: John Edmond
claims.episode_title: An Interview with John Edmond - Luciferous LED Lucubrator

claims.claim_text: Full turnkey outsourcing hides recurring costs: the customer returns with more money each time parts go unsourceable or firmware nobody wrote in-house fails.
claims.quote_verbatim: you know you're going to be coming back with another bag of money in about three months when they can't source those parts anymore or your firmware doesn't work
claims.episode_title: Kickstarter, Manufacturing, Open Hardware - Judging Jurisdictional Junctures

claims.claim_text: There is real value in keeping specific steps of the production line under your own control rather than handing the entire product to an outside house.
claims.quote_verbatim: there is a significant value to having stuff, to having certain parts of the line in your own control
claims.episode_title: Kickstarter, Manufacturing, Open Hardware - Judging Jurisdictional Junctures

claims.claim_text: A company designing its own chips is chasing control and margin, but the real test of integration is whether it owns the underlying instruction-set architecture rather than licensing it.
claims.quote_verbatim: Apple are going that route to get more control. And to squeeze more margin. You do not see them buying ARM.
claims.episode_title: Kickstarter, Open Source RC & Modelsource - Facinorous Financial Foulness

claims.claim_text: Alcatel ran an extreme in-house model, etching its own boards and writing its own board layout software rather than buying either.
claims.quote_verbatim: They did everything in-house from etching their own boards to writing their own board layout software.
claims.speaker: Vincent Himpe
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Vincent Himpe - Escaped Electron Elocution

claims.claim_text: Alcatel peaked at 216,000 employees, with subsidiaries making its capacitors and resistors and its own semiconductor fabs.
claims.quote_verbatim: They have 216,000 employees in the peak.
claims.speaker: Vincent Himpe
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Vincent Himpe - Escaped Electron Elocution

claims.claim_text: Making a critical subsystem such as battery packs yourself means you own the underlying technology and the patents on it, not just the production capacity.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you start to, to crank this stuff out yourself, not only do you own the technology behind it, right? So like the battery packs
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Solar Factories and HVDC Lines - Pollent Power Pushing

claims.claim_text: Owning production converts a supply problem into a manufacturing engineering problem of yield and quality, in exchange for removing delivery risk from outside vendors.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's a manufacturing engineering problem because you, you have to get high quality and high yield and all that other stuff that manufacturing engineers love
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Solar Factories and HVDC Lines - Pollent Power Pushing

claims.claim_text: Western Electric took integration to the raw material level, grinding its own coal for the carbon microphones in telephone handsets and fabricating its own ICs.
claims.quote_verbatim: They used to grind their own coal to make the microphones that went into the phones.
claims.speaker: Dave Vandenbout
claims.episode_title: Impedance Matching" with Davidson and Vandenbout - Presbytes Pushing Portfolios

claims.claim_text: An in-house-only culture becomes a liability when the best available part is external; in 1979 a Bell Labs project had to reach outside for a Motorola 6801 microprocessor.
claims.quote_verbatim: when I started back in 79, we were doing a project and it needed a microprocessor in it. And the one that we selected was the Motorola 6801
claims.speaker: Dave Vandenbout
claims.episode_title: Impedance Matching" with Davidson and Vandenbout - Presbytes Pushing Portfolios

claims.claim_text: A single-site integrated operation typically combines machining with in-house electronics assembly including its own pick and place line.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's very vertically integrated type stuff. You know, a lot of machining, a lot of electronics assembly, stuff like that.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Consolidate All The Things - Zonked Zelotic Zaitech

claims.claim_text: SpaceX treats how much of its parts it makes internally as a point of pride and a deliberate strategic choice rather than an accident of scale.
claims.quote_verbatim: like I was at SpaceX and they talk about it. They talk about, they're proud of how vertically integrated they are.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Inspirations and Aspirations - Recanting Rocket Rationale

claims.claim_text: A dedicated in-house line is a miniature form of integration: parts stay on hand, feeders stay loaded, and the process is already proven.
claims.quote_verbatim: that is a miniaturized version of vertically integrated in that those parts will definitely be on hand. Those machines are definitely set up for this process.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Inspirations and Aspirations - Recanting Rocket Rationale

claims.claim_text: Unless you own the end-user installation step, customers will mix and match identified parts however they like, so the best defense is a system that detects and flags the mismatch.
claims.quote_verbatim: unless you have a completely integrated, like, like tightly regulated system where you are doing the full, like the full, fully folded, vertically integrated, where you're doing the actual end user integration as well, then you're always going to have people use it however they want to
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ronald Sousa of Hash Define Electronics

claims.claim_text: Domestic in-house manufacturing survives mainly in higher-margin niches such as telecom equipment, where the margin covers the cost of keeping the line at home.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've talked to folks that are from that scene still today that are building, you know, telecom equipment or like stuff that's probably higher margins, um, to where they can afford to do that domestic manufacturing in-house
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Large firms genuinely evaluate acquiring a supplier as a remedy for an obsolete part, because at multi-billion-dollar scale the purchase price is affordable relative to a redesign.
claims.quote_verbatim: you have an obsolete part and sometimes it's like, well, we should just buy the company
claims.episode_title: Documentation Is A Waste Of Time

claims.claim_text: Without owning the board house, compressing turnaround means paying substantial expedite fees, which sets a floor on how fast an outsourced prototype service can quote.
claims.quote_verbatim: unless you're so vertically integrated that you own your own board house, you start to incur some pretty substantial costs in expedited fees
claims.speaker: Jonathan Hirschman
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jonathan Hirschman of PCB:NG

claims.claim_text: Board houses quote in working days while customers experience calendar days, so holidays silently stretch any lead time promised to the end customer.
claims.quote_verbatim: the board houses, they do not work on calendar days. They work on working days. So that's part of the issue.
claims.speaker: Jonathan Hirschman
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jonathan Hirschman of PCB:NG

claims.claim_text: PCB:NG standardized on a 12 calendar day promise as the balance point between speed and price for assembled prototypes.
claims.quote_verbatim: we just call it 12 calendar days, which is actually fairly, fairly aggressive compared to what's out there
claims.speaker: Jonathan Hirschman
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jonathan Hirschman of PCB:NG

claims.claim_text: Hearing aid manufacturers have been buying up the retail shops that dispense their devices, integrating forward all the way to the end user.
claims.quote_verbatim: the company that runs the hearing aids are also eating up some of the shops that actually are selling the devices that way
claims.speaker: Jørgen Jakobsen

claims.claim_text: An integrated EDA data flow only works if every component vendor supplies data for it, and vendors that sell into many tool ecosystems supply it inconsistently or not at all.
claims.quote_verbatim: having vertical integration where like if if you can actually get every vendor to go for that then maybe right but more than likely they're they have to play multiple fiddles as well
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A one-person product company can be effectively integrated by owning design, firmware and assembly, including running a pick and place machine in a garage.
claims.quote_verbatim: I basically am pretty much fully vertically integrated as people would call it. It's including having a pick and place machine in the garage
claims.speaker: Piotr Esden-Tempski

claims.claim_text: The Shenzhen manufacturing model is a dense mesh of small hyper-specialized firms partnering with each other, in contrast to the American instinct to grow one firm that owns every step.
claims.quote_verbatim: the Shenzhen ecosystem is at least at the level that I engage with is a lot of very, a lot of small companies all working together very closely rather than a couple of big manufacturers
claims.speaker: Scotty Allen

claims.claim_text: Even the largest contract manufacturers subcontract work out to small and medium specialist shops, so apparent integration at the top hides a fragmented supplier base.
claims.quote_verbatim: And there are big, I mean, there's Foxconn and things like that. But a lot of them sub out too, right?
claims.speaker: Scotty Allen

claims.claim_text: Past a certain company size, making your own components stops being a strategic decision and becomes the default outcome.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you're that huge of quite, it's, you know, it's a foregone conclusion that you're going to end up making your own, you know, stuff
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Owning both the hardware and the software organizations produces a better joint result than contracting either out, because the interface between them can be negotiated internally.
claims.quote_verbatim: the more you're integrated vertically, the better you can get of the marriage of software and hardware
claims.speaker: Shahriar Shahramian

claims.claim_text: The common high-volume arrangement is bare boards fabbed offsite but SMT and final assembly co-located at one site.
claims.quote_verbatim: the bare boards are fabbed, uh, offsite, but then they're brought onsite and then SMT and final assembly are co-located
claims.speaker: Chrissy Meyer

claims.claim_text: Co-locating SMT with final assembly matters because board-level defects always surface on the final assembly line and engineers need to physically walk between the two.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're always going to find board level problems on a final assembly line and, uh, being able to run back and forth, I think is, is super critical
claims.speaker: Chrissy Meyer

claims.claim_text: Campus-style integration puts injection molding, camera module assembly and cable build within a building or two of final assembly, which is how firms like DJI reach efficiencies hard to match elsewhere.
claims.quote_verbatim: not just will my final assembly and SMT happen at the same place, like the same company or the next building over will be injection molding all of my plastic parts
claims.speaker: Chrissy Meyer

claims.claim_text: China shifted over roughly a decade from being the place to set up a supply chain and build to a design and engineering base of integrated firms.
claims.quote_verbatim: when I first started traveling to China over a decade ago, like China was the place you'd go to build stuff, like set up a supply chain and build stuff
claims.speaker: Chrissy Meyer

claims.claim_text: A network operator model installs and owns the low-power base stations and sells connectivity as a service, whereas an alliance-based radio standard leaves deployment to a heterogeneous set of independent network companies.
claims.quote_verbatim: So LoRaWAN is not... They're not as vertically integrated. I mean, it's a technology. It's an alliance.

claims.claim_text: Shipping the host computer alongside the instrument removes the version-dependency failures that plague software running on unknown customer machines, at a high cost per unit.
claims.quote_verbatim: The best case scenario for like shipping a product would be also to ship them a computer that it is destined to work with. Like vertical integration is really expensive, but damn, if it doesn't work every time
claims.speaker: Jean Rintoul

claims.claim_text: Chinese factories commonly hold SMT, injection molding, mold making, final assembly, test and packaging under one roof, which is the biggest structural difference from other regions.
claims.quote_verbatim: China tends to be very vertically integrated in that you'll have the, uh, SMT, uh, injection molding, maybe even mold making final assembly test packaging all under one roof
claims.speaker: Scott Miller

claims.claim_text: US and European manufacturing is typically horizontal, so a product may need one EMS for SMT, another for molding and a third for assembly, raising the effort of stitching a supply chain together.
claims.quote_verbatim: in the U S and Europe, it is typically much more horizontal. So you might have one, um, EMS that does the SMT, another one does the molding, and then you may have to find a third one to, um, assemble the parts
claims.speaker: Scott Miller

claims.claim_text: A horizontal supplier base costs more coordination but rewards firms that build databases of which factories work well together and already have payment terms in place.
claims.quote_verbatim: it takes a lot more effort to put together your supply chain because it's not, you know, one throat to choke or one, one stop
claims.speaker: Scott Miller

claims.claim_text: A tightly optimized in-house flow, such as scripts that pull the BOM and program the pick and place directly, makes any deviation from the standard process an entire project rather than a small change.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you move outside of this process that you're really normal and used to, then there's going to be, there's going to be problems and, you know, issues and stuff like that. And, and really just time.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Teardown cost estimates capture only chip prices; the real cost of an integrated product includes assembly, transportation and warehousing.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you want the real cost, you have to factor in all the assembly and transportation and other warehousing
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Moving into custom silicon is unlike adding custom mechanical parts, because a new die has to go through the entire process rather than reusing tooling the way plastics and stamping do.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's not like they're just, you know, turning around and spinning up a, you know, a stamping plant that, or, you know, they cut a new die to do a new chip. They have to actually go all the way through the process.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Owning manufacturing is close to a structural requirement in the automotive sector, not a distinguishing strategy of any one carmaker.
claims.quote_verbatim: A lot of other car companies are all, you know, vertically integrated in that way, too. It just feels like it's almost a necessity.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Carmakers have pushed integration back to raw materials, with land or mines bought to secure lithium supply.
claims.quote_verbatim: Well, they actually just bought a lithium mine or something. Or they bought land that has lithium on it.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Tektronix became integrated to the point that engineers could order custom desks built internally, an example of integration extending past anything strategically useful.
claims.quote_verbatim: in Tektronix, it was so vertically integrated, you would call down to get your desk built custom
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The supplier margin you eliminate by owning a step was payment for that supplier solving problems on your behalf and for your ability to shop around, so both disappear with the margin.
claims.quote_verbatim: the margin that you pay them is them solving problems for you and, like, being able to shop around
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The accounting case for owning a step is deceptively simple, since the saved payment to the outside vendor is visible while the costs you absorb are not.
claims.quote_verbatim: hey, well, we could save even more if we don't have to give this money to the capacitor manufacturer. We're the capacitor manufacturer. But there's a lot of hidden downsides to doing that
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Heavy integration drifts toward everything being custom, including custom alloys, and that steady move away from standard parts creates its own long-run problem.
claims.quote_verbatim: moving so far away from standardization, it becomes problematic
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A distributed firmware update path only works if every module in the chain implements the update mechanism, which is far easier to guarantee when one company owns all the modules.
claims.quote_verbatim: even if you have a new ABS module, then you have to go through all these layers up and all of them need to support this, this firmware update mechanism
claims.speaker: Joris Aerts
claims.episode_title: Satellites and EVs with Joris Aerts

claims.claim_text: User experience control is one driver of walled-garden integration, but it cannot be the only one, since launch-vehicle firms integrate just as hard with no consumer experience at stake.
claims.quote_verbatim: Well, but if you look at SpaceX, they don't really care about their user experience. So there must be something else that's also driving this vertical integration
claims.speaker: Joris Aerts
claims.episode_title: Satellites and EVs with Joris Aerts

claims.claim_text: Specifying a submodule to a third party can be self-defeating when the technology moves faster than the spec, build and test cycle, so the delivered part is already behind.
claims.quote_verbatim: it has to do with technology moving so fast that by the time, you know, you finish your spec for your third party to, to build your, your sub module that by the time it's done and tested, technology has already moved on
claims.speaker: Joris Aerts
claims.episode_title: Satellites and EVs with Joris Aerts

claims.claim_text: Owning your production concentrates risk: a downturn in your single industry leaves the capacity idle, whereas a merchant module supplier spreads that exposure across markets.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're much more at risk for if your specific industry goes down, then you have all this manufacturing capacity sitting idle
claims.speaker: Joris Aerts
claims.episode_title: Satellites and EVs with Joris Aerts

claims.claim_text: Bringing a step in-house requires enough revenue at the back end to fund the scale, which is why small companies cannot pursue it even when it would help them technically.
claims.quote_verbatim: There's enough money at the back end, which is what you really need to get scale. If you can't get that money, then yeah, you're not going to, that vertical integration doesn't happen with small companies.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Satellites and EVs with Joris Aerts

claims.claim_text: Owning every layer removes much of the need for formal specifications and standards, because the interfaces are internal and can be changed without negotiating across organizations.
claims.quote_verbatim: vertical integration basically removes some of the need for this sort of like the need to communicate between organizations, the less need for standard
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Simulating Embedded Hardware with Michael Gielda

claims.claim_text: Open source tooling lets a small firm integrate its whole toolchain without owning the vendors, achieving the benefits of integration while others validate the code.
claims.quote_verbatim: because of using open source technology, we can have infinite amount of vertical integration
claims.speaker: Michael Gielda
claims.episode_title: Simulating Embedded Hardware with Michael Gielda

claims.claim_text: An integrated IoT platform feels effortless because it hides every layer, but the price is that leaving the ecosystem means restarting the project from scratch.
claims.quote_verbatim: that magical thing is magical because it's vertically integrated, right? They've taken care of everything under the hood, but you either have to stay in their ecosystem, pay for their ecosystem
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Why IoT Is Difficult with Jonathan Beri

claims.claim_text: Standardizing on a shared instruction set architecture for cost reasons pushes the industry away from single-company silicon stacks and toward parts that cross vendor boundaries.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think that that's, that helps to build instead of like these vertically integrated companies, it starts to build more like crossover type stuff.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Building a competitive programmable-logic product requires developing hardware, software and architecture together, which effectively demands direct control of the whole stack.
claims.quote_verbatim: you have to harness both hardware software and architecture concurrently to build something good that's where the core is

claims.claim_text: An EDA vendor took an equity stake in a contract manufacturer after previously acquiring another one, a common pattern where investment gives visibility into the books ahead of a possible purchase.
claims.quote_verbatim: Usually that's like a, that's like them lining up the shot to eventually buy Macrofab. Right. They did with PCBNG.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Linking a design tool to a factory allows manufacturing data to be pushed back into the layout, so issues like heat shadowing from a capacitor too close to a BGA surface during design rather than at build.
claims.quote_verbatim: you could basically have a manufacturer comment like, Oh, Hey, that BGA is going to have some shadowing, some heat shadowing because it's a little bit too close to one of the caps
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: An integrated manufacturer can change a design without renegotiating with an outside supplier, whereas contracts with third-party manufacturers often penalize changes outright.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're not putting, going external to the company and being like, oh, actually, you know, third party manufacturer, we need you to change this spec
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Owning the whole product encourages designers to merge USB, video and audio into one proprietary connector, which saves connectors on the product but strands users without standard cables.
claims.quote_verbatim: we don't use separate connectors. We can use one and we can share USB and we can share the video output and we can share the audio output
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Some organizations run an internal chip fab purely to keep intellectual property from leaving the building rather than for cost or capacity reasons.
claims.quote_verbatim: they have their own in-house chip fab because they don't want the IP to go out anywhere else. They don't want it to leave the wall.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Demand at specialty foundries may grow from carmakers deciding they must own their silicon, rather than from traditional chip companies that are consolidating into each other.
claims.quote_verbatim: Intel may be getting into the foundry business, but I think there is going to be more, more market for a global foundries, or even like the skywaters of the world to expand more
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Designing your own chips without owning fabs is a partial form of integration; the silicon still comes from a foundry with all the scheduling dependence that implies.
claims.quote_verbatim: They're designing their own, but they're not making them.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: An analog chip company outsourcing not just fabrication but its process technology to a foundry lowers operating budgets while surrendering the process advantage that was its moat.
claims.quote_verbatim: I was not a fan as people remember when, when analog devices talked about outsourcing a lot of their stuff to TSMC. They even said the process technology, we're just going to do what they do.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Tight size, weight and power constraints make off-the-shelf components hard to fit, pushing robotics designs toward integrated in-house hardware.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're really constrained in those regards, it's harder to integrate off the shelf components and you need to go to a more embedded and integrated design

claims.claim_text: There is a market gap between building everything in house and buying off-the-shelf parts designed for other markets, which is where purpose-built component suppliers position themselves.
claims.quote_verbatim: I saw this gap in the market between, you know, building everything in house yourself or buying things off the shelf that were designed for other markets

claims.claim_text: No realistic company spans silicon design through cloud software, so engineers necessarily depend on interfaces they do not understand internally.
claims.quote_verbatim: you would have to work at such a massive company that is so vertically integrated that you have, you have a silicon designer all the way up to someone writing software on a cloud server
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Some semiconductor startups are explicitly founded on the premise of owning the entire process from raw silicon upward because the parts they need cannot be bought.
claims.quote_verbatim: if we can't buy the stuff we need, we're going to make it, you know, and they want to own the entire process from start from raw silicon
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Headcount figures understate the real size of a product organization, because an unintegrated company does not employ the contract manufacturer building its hardware.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you look at like all of the stuff, all of like the, the layers and layers and layers of going to an iPhone and similar, it's massive
claims.episode_title: Moving Down The Stack with Scott Williams

claims.claim_text: If a chip company owned the EDA tools, competing silicon vendors would refuse to design in tools controlled by a rival, which limits how far up the value chain a component maker can integrate.
claims.quote_verbatim: the competitors in the silicon space would then be upset because it would be like, well, now our design tools are owned by our competitor
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Newer electric vehicle makers converge on a small number of platform variants, differing mainly by battery stacking and motor sizing, which pairs naturally with owning the whole build.
claims.quote_verbatim: But then I think they have different options within that battery family. You know, maybe they double stack the batteries.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Outsourced aerospace programs slip schedule because requirements flow down through many subcontractors, whereas keeping the build in-house has protected timelines.
claims.quote_verbatim: the modern kind of outsourced manufacturing thing of just like schedule slippage because you have so many subcontractors, so many like requirements docs that are like flowing down the line
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Owning factories and staff is a cash-heavy operation with non-trivial carrying costs, which is why it is abandoned first, though in safety-critical industries the cost of quality and returns can justify keeping it.
claims.quote_verbatim: the carrying costs of all the people and the factories and the – you know, all that kind of stuff. Like that is very non-trivial. It's a very cash-heavy kind of operation.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: CircuitHub began as a software network layered on other companies' factories and only opened its own facility in 2017, using common off-the-shelf equipment wrapped in software.
claims.quote_verbatim: we started off with this, this network model on top of other people's factories. We actually set up our first whole home factory back in 2017.
claims.speaker: Andrew Seddon
claims.episode_title: CircuitHub, 12 Years Later with Andrew Seddon

claims.claim_text: An integrated prototype and small-batch electronics facility can be built by importing semiconductor fab techniques into board assembly rather than copying conventional EMS practice.
claims.quote_verbatim: We've taken a lot of the techniques that originate in semiconductor fabrication, which is like one of the most advanced manufacturing processes on the planet
claims.speaker: Andrew Seddon
claims.episode_title: CircuitHub, 12 Years Later with Andrew Seddon

claims.claim_text: The Starlink factory in Texas covers bare PCB fabrication, surface mount, functional test, injection molding and CNC box build in one site, shipping roughly a thousand finished units a day.
claims.quote_verbatim: they do everything from, uh, PCB fabrications. So they're making the bare PCBs. They're doing all of the surface mount, they're doing functional tests that they're doing the injection molding, CNC box build assembly
claims.speaker: Andrew Seddon
claims.episode_title: CircuitHub, 12 Years Later with Andrew Seddon

claims.claim_text: Losing domestic prototyping capacity costs a country the ability to iterate products rapidly, because much product innovation originates from observations made on the manufacturing floor.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you lose the ability to prototype in your home country, you lose the ability to do rapid product iteration
claims.speaker: Andrew Seddon
claims.episode_title: CircuitHub, 12 Years Later with Andrew Seddon

claims.claim_text: Throwing a product over the wall to an outside manufacturer degrades the design itself, since design improvements often come from spotting problems during the build.
claims.quote_verbatim: you have to have a deep understanding of the manufacturing process, because often as you're making these, these products, you'll spot something that happens in manufacturing that you then feed back into the
claims.speaker: Andrew Seddon
claims.episode_title: CircuitHub, 12 Years Later with Andrew Seddon

claims.claim_text: Domestic volume manufacturing of a commodity consumer product remains viable with sustained automation and process optimization, as with a UK vacuum maker holding about half its home market.
claims.quote_verbatim: about half of the market is these, is these Henry Hoovers and they're actually made in the UK
claims.speaker: Andrew Seddon
claims.episode_title: CircuitHub, 12 Years Later with Andrew Seddon

claims.claim_text: Much of the remaining electronics and mechanical shop base is owned by operators near retirement, which has fed private equity roll-ups of PCB fab and assembly capacity.
claims.quote_verbatim: they are owned by people that are kind of looking to retire pretty soon. And, you know, they might consider some sales to, to private equity.
claims.speaker: Andrew Seddon
claims.episode_title: CircuitHub, 12 Years Later with Andrew Seddon

claims.claim_text: Commercial CAD suites are built as integrated stacks so the vendor can sell the entire solution including signal integrity add-ons, whereas an open tool stays flat and separable.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's not vertically integrated like a lot of, a lot of CAD programs are right. Because they're built by big companies for big companies. And so they're vertically integrated. Like they want you to buy the whole solution.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
